_README: What each of the workbook's nine MPs does on their turn, by opp_id.
A BRIDGE, AND A TEMPORARY ONE, exactly like modifier_effects.json. The
right home for these is an 'Intent pattern' column in the workbook next
to the element pair, and Cameron has been asked to approve one. Until he
does, opponents.json is regenerated by export_data.py on every run and
would throw away anything written into it by hand, so the patterns live
here instead.
The code reads the workbook column FIRST and only falls back to this, so
the day the column lands this file stops being consulted and can be
deleted.
WRITTEN BY HAND. export_data.py never overwrites it.
NOTE ON WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT AFFECT. These nine are reached
through modules.json. The six playtest levels fight thirteen separate
placeholder opponents whose patterns are written inline in levels.json,
so changing a number here does not change a playtest.
THE FIVE PATTERNS, from Cameron on 2026-09-21. A move is a verb and
either one number or a range to roll between, inclusive at both ends.
A move that comes out at zero is not taken — the opponent steps to the
next move and does that instead, so pattern 4 never guards at all.
1  attack 1-6 / gain 1-6 / block 0-2   wildly variable, rarely defends
2  attack 4   / gain 0-1 / block 3-5   steady pressure behind a guard
3  attack 0-6 / gain 2-4 / block 1-3   unpredictable, builds steadily
4  attack 5   / gain 0-2 / block 0     relentless, never defends
5  attack 1-3 / gain 3-5 / block 4     turtles and grows its support
ASSIGNED ROUND-ROBIN, and deliberately arbitrary. Cameron asked for the
five to be spread across the nine without regard to who they are; the
'AI style' prose that used to describe each MP has been deleted, and
opponent character will be rebuilt from these numbers plus on-screen
verbal cues in a later build. Changing one of these is one line.
